statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-85977: a client that calls pmap_getmaps() against an attacker-controlled host can be driven into unbounded memory and CPU use by a crafted PMAPPROC_DUMP reply (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-85977, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2478979). Upstream fixed it in libtirpc commit ccc1acf867d88dc0bdbe58568f621607d44977f5 (https://git.linux-nfs.org/cgit/steved/libtirpc.git/commit/?id=ccc1acf867d88dc0bdbe58568f621607d44977f5), which caps the number of list nodes decoded by xdr_pmaplist(), xdr_rpcblist_ptr() and xdr_rpcb_entry_list_ptr() in src/pmap_prot2.c and src/rpcb_prot.c at 1024. Debian lists trixie 1.3.6+ds-1 as vulnerable (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85977). The DHI Debian repository publishes two builds of Debian's libtirpc 1.3.6+ds-1 for Debian 13. Checked in the shared library libtirpc.so.3.0.0 (libtirpc3t64) of both builds on amd64 and arm64: in the second build, each of xdr_pmaplist(), xdr_rpcblist_ptr() and xdr_rpcb_entry_list_ptr() compares its decoded-node count with 1024, as the upstream commit adds, and in the first build none of them has that comparison. The second build's changelog records the backport and the first build's does not. The first build is affected; the range ends at the second.
